Local SEO in 2026 is defined by a three-surface evaluation model where Google analyzes **Local Map Pack results, Local Organic results, and AI-generated local recommendations** (also known as Generative Engine Optimization or GEO) [1, 2]. While traditional factors like distance still constrain rankings, the emphasis has shifted toward **entity-based authority** and verified real-world activity [3, 4].

### Local Map Pack Ranking Factors (2026)
According to industry experts, Map Pack rankings are driven by three core pillars: **Relevance, Distance, and Prominence** [5-7]. In 2026, the weighted influence of ranking signals for the Local Pack is distributed as follows:
*   **Google Business Profile (GBP) Signals (32%):** Categories, profile completeness, and freshness [8, 9].
*   **Review Signals (20%):** Volume, velocity, and sentiment [9, 10].
*   **On-Page Signals (15%):** NAP presence, location-specific keywords, and domain authority [9, 10].
*   **Behavioral Signals (9%):** Click-through rates, mobile "clicks to call," and direction requests [9, 10].
*   **Link Signals (8%):** Local backlinks and brand authority [9, 11].
*   **Citation Signals (6%):** Consistent business data across directories [9, 11].

### Google Business Profile Optimization
A complete GBP is the single most influential asset for local SEO, with 46% of all Google searches carrying local intent [12-14].
*   **Primary Category:** This is the strongest individual ranking signal; you must select the most specific match (e.g., "Personal Injury Attorney" instead of "Lawyer") to maximize relevance [8, 15-17].
*   **Photo Strategy:** While some sources suggest a minimum of **10–25 high-quality photos** [13, 18, 19], vendor research from Google (cited by Fuel Online) claims profiles with **100+ photos** generate **520% more calls** than those with fewer than 10 [20, 21].
*   **Posting Cadence:** You should publish **1–3 Google Posts weekly** [13, 16]. Posts now surface in AI Overview citations and Discover feeds, making frequency more important than length [22, 23].
*   **Q&A Seeding:** Owners should proactively seed **8–12 questions** that customers frequently ask (e.g., pricing, service areas) to feed AI answer engines [24-26].

### Reviews and Review Velocity
Reviews are no longer just for social proof; they are structured data that AI models use to understand business context [27, 28].
*   **Velocity Thresholds:** Aim for a steady cadence of **2–4 new reviews per week** [29]. A consistent volume of **5–15 reviews per month** for six months can jump a business 5–10 positions in the Map Pack [13, 30].
*   **AI Citations:** A study by vendor **GrowthPro AI** indicates businesses with **50+ reviews** in the past 12 months are **3x more likely** to appear in AI recommendations [31]. They also found that maintaining a **4.5+ star rating** leads to being cited **2x more often** by AI tools [31].
*   **Semantic Content:** Google parses review text for specific service mentions and locations [32, 33]. Responses to reviews should be personalized and completed within **24–48 hours** [25, 28, 30].

### NAP Citations and Local Authority
Consistency in **Name, Address, and Phone number (NAP)** remains a foundational trust signal [34-36].
*   **Consistency:** Minor discrepancies (e.g., "St." vs. "Street") can confuse search engines and suppress rankings [36, 37].
*   **Tiered Strategy:** Focus first on **Tier 1 "Giants"** (Google, Bing Places, Apple Maps, Yelp, Facebook), followed by data aggregators (Data Axle, Localeze), and then industry-specific directories (e.g., Avvo for lawyers) [38, 39].
*   **Tools:** Use **BrightLocal, Whitespark, or Yext** to automate citation management and audit for duplicates [40-43].

### Local Landing Pages
Dedicated pages for every location and service are essential for capturing high-intent organic traffic [44-46].
*   **Hyperlocal Content:** Each page must feature unique content, including local landmarks, neighborhood-specific proof, and city-specific testimonials [45, 47-49].
*   **Schema Markup:** Implement **LocalBusiness, Service, and FAQPage schema** [50-53]. Pages with **FAQ schema** are **4x more likely** to be cited in Google AI Overviews [54].
*   **Performance:** A site must load in **under two seconds** on mobile to avoid suppressing local rankings [52, 55].

### Service Area Businesses (SABs)
SABs face unique rules in 2026, as Google is phasing out hybrid storefront/SAB listings [22].
*   **Address Privacy:** If operating from a residential location, you **must hide the public address** while defining a specific Service Area by city or ZIP code [56-58].
*   **Service Radius:** Boundaries should generally not extend beyond **40 miles** or **two hours of driving time** from the base of operations [57, 59].

### AI Search and Local Discovery (GEO/AEO)
Local discovery is moving from "blue links" to "intelligent answers" [4].
*   **AIO Prevalence:** There is disagreement on the frequency of Google AI Overviews (AIO). One survey notes they appear on **23% of searches** [60], while a **BrightEdge/Ahrefs** study (cited by vendor Reporter Outreach) puts the figure at **48%** [61, 62]. A separate study by **Seer Interactive** claims AIOs now show up on **over 83% of all queries** [63].
*   **Positional Bias:** Research on LLMs shows a "lost in the middle" effect; **44.2% of citations** originate from the **first 30% of source text** [64, 65]. Tactics should involve placing authority-signaling answers in the first 150 words of a landing page [66, 67].
*   **Entity Confidence:** AI tools are **67% more likely** to cite a business if its entity definition is consistent across **10+ platforms** [68].
*   **Zero-Click Reality:** Roughly **93% of AI Mode queries** result in zero clicks to external websites (based on a **Seer Interactive** analysis of 25.1M impressions), making appearing in the AI summary the primary goal [61, 69].
